name: Capsule Technologies
old_description: Philips Capsule is now part of the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio of solutions – a comprehensive, clinically focused ecosystem designed to enhance care delivery across the healthcare enterprise, with a goal of improving patient outcomes and reducing clinician burnout.
about:
Capsule Technologies, now operating as Philips Capsule within the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio, is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company was acquired by Philips and integrated into its acute care informatics division; its founding year and original founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The company develops vendor‑neutral medical device integration and clinical informatics software. Its platform captures live‑streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices and delivers it to more than 100 downstream systems, including electronic health records, alarm management, and research databases. The portfolio spans medical device integration (Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress), a medical device information platform, virtual care management (eCareManager), retrospective analytics (Clinical Insights Manager), clinical surveillance (Capsule Surveillance), and a critical care clinical information system (IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia).

Customers are hospitals and health systems worldwide. Named references include Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. The solutions target acute care, perioperative, and virtual care environments.

The company emphasizes a vendor‑neutral, open ecosystem that works with existing infrastructure, deep clinical and operational experience to fit workflows, and a track record of measurable outcomes such as time savings and a seven‑year run of positive Net Promoter Scores.
